name: Pelindo

stores_or_sites: 17 subsidiaries listed on Wikipedia (several are terminal operators)
fit_rationale: State port monopoly with no consumer audience; F1 value would be B2B hospitality for shipping lines and investors around Indonesia's port privatisation and terminal partnerships, a weak fit.

name: Freeport Indonesia
desc: Operator of the Grasberg copper and gold mine in Papua and a copper smelter in Gresik, majority owned by the Indonesian state.
products: copper concentrate and cathode, gold, silver
parent_immediate: PT Mineral Industri Indonesia (MIND ID) 41.23% plus PT Indonesia Papua Metal & Mineral 10%; Freeport-McMoRan 48.77%
stores_or_sites: Grasberg mine (Papua); smelter in Gresik Special Economic Zone, East Java
markets: sells copper and gold from Indonesia to domestic and international buyers

alt_indicators.evidence: 2025 sales volume 1.2 billion pounds of copper and 1.1 million ounces of gold
Total contributions to the state of IDR 75 trillion including 2025 net profit share; dividends to MIND ID IDR 16.9 trillion
2023 production 680,000 tonnes of copper and 52.9 tonnes of gold

profitability_basis: company page refers to the 2025 net profit share distributed in April 2026
distress: September 2025 landslide at the mine killed seven workers; company says production is around 40-50% with a return to full capacity targeted by early 2028 (ptfi.co.id, 7 May 2026)

signals.what: Production at 40-50% after accident; full capacity targeted by early 2028

fit_rationale: Commodity miner selling copper and gold to refiners; little commercial reason to buy F1 rights beyond state-image or investor hospitality, and a fatal 2025 accident weighs on reputation.
compliance: Fatal mine accident September 2025; long-running Papua social and environmental controversies (not researched further).
outstanding: No revenue figure for PTFI itself; employees not found.
discovery_source: candidate named from researcher's own knowledge (no list page); checked with check.py

name: Insular Life
aliases: The Insular Life Assurance Company, Ltd.
desc: Policyholder-owned Philippine mutual life insurer, the country's first Filipino life insurer, offering life, health and group benefits.
products: life insurance, group benefits, health cover
marketing_autonomy_basis: independent mutual with its own board and management
qualifying_metric: revenue (FY2020, flagged as older than three years); total assets PHP 148.7bn
profitability_basis: net income PHP 3.14bn in 2020 (Wikipedia, citing annual report)

signals.what: Agreed to acquire 100% of Generali's Philippine life subsidiary; completed after regulatory approval in May 2025
Sold Insular Health Care to Value-Based Health Care (Singapore)
Rebranded the acquired Generali unit as InLife Benefits

fit_rationale: Acquisitive mutual insurer rebranding its group-benefits arm; F1 hospitality could serve corporate group-benefit clients, but the business is Philippines-only and the fit is modest.

access.roles: President and CEO; Executive Chairperson; head of marketing (not named)

outstanding: Latest financials found are FY2020; premiums and newer results not verified.
